speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly what you felt when it started, such as a spinning sensation or just dizziness? Did you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea at the same time?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The description of a brief (3-minute) spinning sensation with nausea, occurring suddenly at rest and resolving completely, is highly characteristic of BPPV. Did you notice that the spinning started specifically when you turned your head or changed position in bed? I will also request a Dix-Hallpike test result to confirm the diagnosis.
